glue6.name: Glue on 6.0
glue6.summary: Serverless ETL billed per second at $0.308 per DPU-hour on Glue 6.0 and above.
glue6.bestWhen: you run scheduled ETL on AWS and want no servers.
glue6.watchOut: jobs pinned to Glue 5.1 or older keep the $0.44 rate, the default is 10 DPUs, and you should test a 5.1 job before moving it.

flex.name: Glue Flex
flex.summary: Glue jobs on spare capacity at $0.29 per DPU-hour, or $0.203 on Glue 6.0.
flex.watchOut: start and run times vary, capacity can be reclaimed, and Flex does not support Python Shell, streaming or ML jobs.

athena.name: Amazon Athena
athena.summary: SQL queries on data in S3, billed by data scanned or compute used.
athena.bestWhen: your job is really a SQL question on files already in S3.
athena.watchOut: one reviewer says it can get costly if analysts do not know partition keys, and AWS's own example shows file layout changes the bill a lot.

emr.name: Amazon EMR
emr.summary: Big data clusters you configure, or EMR Serverless, billed per second with a 1-minute minimum.
emr.bestWhen: you want to pick the servers and tune Spark yourself.
emr.watchOut: on EC2 clusters you choose and pay for the servers underneath, so the setup work is yours.

other.name: Neither: look at another tool
other.summary: A tool built to capture database changes, since Glue's zero-ETL for self-managed databases only lands in Redshift.
other.bestWhen: you need database changes landed in Iceberg tables.
other.watchOut: we found no Glue page that documents log-based change data capture for self-managed databases, so compare tools first.
